abstract: This study investigated inflammation-associated microglial states, cross-glial inflammatory signaling and spinal myelin abnormalities after CCI, and evaluated their response to BoNT/A administered after pain hypersensitivity had developed. Male rats underwent CCI and received intrathecal BoNT/A on D7. Behavioral phenotyping was integrated with spinal transcriptomics, proteomics, scRNA-seq, Western blotting, immunofluorescence, TEM, conditioned-medium transfer, TNF-α challenge, and in vitro and in vivo IL-1β add-back. CCI produced persistent mechanical, thermal, and cold hypersensitivity together with shifts in inflammation-associated microglial states and transcriptional programs, increased spinal NF-κB/NLRP3-caspase-1-IL-1β-related proteins, an enhanced C3-associated astrocytic response, and abnormalities in OLIG/OPC states and myelin structure. BoNT/A attenuated inflammatory readouts, was associated with higher OLIG2 and MBP signals, and reduced the apparent severity of myelin ultrastructural abnormalities. Single-cell analyses described cell-state patterns, while CellChat prioritized candidate microglia-astrocyte interactions. Conditioned medium from LPS-stimulated microglia increased astrocytic C3, whereas BoNT/A pretreatment reduced this effect; IL-1β add-back increased C3 and attenuated OLIG2/MBP improvement. TNF-α challenge increased several inflammatory readouts despite continued BoNT/A exposure. BoNT/A given after hypersensitivity onset dampened spinal inflammation and improved myelin-related measures. IL-1β add-back supported a functional link between the inflammatory glial milieu and C3/OLIG2/MBP.

summary: Multi-omic and scRNA-seq profiling of spinal glia after CCI neuropathic pain; BoNT/A dampens inflammation and improves myelin markers in rats.
title: Multi-omic profiling reveals coordinated remodeling of inflammatory glial states and oligodendrocyte-myelin homeostasis by BoNT/A in CCI-induced neuropathic pain.
